pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business profile is adequate: large and scaled in work where few firms compete, but concentrated in a handful of big fixed-price public projects. Last-twelve-months revenue is USD 6,254,126 thousand, public agencies were 73.82% of nine-month 2026 revenue, and two customers with multiple projects made up 24.1% of it, at 13.3% and 10.8%; the third-quarter report names the second customer, so the earlier Business & governance figure of one customer at 10.8% understates concentration. Management says fewer firms now bid on the largest civil projects, which helps pricing but cannot be tested because no market-share figure is supplied. A funding delay or a dispute on one large project therefore moves earnings and cash more than the revenue base suggests, so scale is a strength and concentration is the matching weakness. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 44, 49–50; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 124; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C8

Revenue is visible for about three years, but the pipeline that feeds it has stopped growing. Nine-month 2026 new awards of USD 4,540.3 million were 0.96x revenue recognised, against USD 7.0 billion in the same period of 2025, and backlog is down 5.77% on a year earlier although up from USD 19.9 billion at the end of the second quarter. Firm remaining performance obligations, which exclude unexercised options, are USD 17.4 billion, 2.78x revenue and down only 2.79% on a year earlier, so the firm base is steadier than the headline backlog. Management attributes the fall to an unusually strong 2025 and fewer large awards reaching decision in 2026, and points to a pipeline above USD 200 billion over three to four years and a multi-billion-dollar California healthcare project to be added within two years; these are expectations, not bookings. Backlog equal to 3.25 years of revenue protects earnings in the near term, but sustained awards below revenue would shrink it and the customer advances attached to it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 49–50, 52–53, 58; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C9

Margin recovery is real but comes from volume and lower stock-linked pay rather than better gross margins, so it is less secure than the headline suggests. Income from construction operations moved from a margin of -2.40% in FY2024 to 4.18% in FY2025 and 6.37% in the first nine months of 2026, yet gross margin was 12.37% against 12.38% a year earlier; of the USD 120,487 thousand rise in operating income, 72.69% came from higher gross profit on 17.62% more revenue and the rest from lower general and administrative cost as share-based pay fell by USD 43.5 million. Civil earned a 14.0% margin against 4.8% in Building and 2.1% in Specialty Contractors, so Civil execution carries the credit. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 42–43, 47, 55–60; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5

Disputes are a recurring cost of this business model, not a one-off, and unproven claims decide how much profit turns into cash. Legal judgments and settlements cost USD 213.5 million in FY2024 and USD 94.3 million in FY2025, which is 40.65% of FY2025 income from construction operations, and a USD 16.4 million adverse change on a California transit project in the first quarter of 2026 came from change-order negotiations that management says were later settled with the owner and should bring cash. Fixed-price work was 79% of backlog at the end of 2025, and claims plus unapproved change orders of USD 687,916 thousand are 89.64% of the USD 767,432 thousand of costs in excess of billings and 136.43% of general-purpose cash, with management expecting about USD 521.4 million of that balance to be collected beyond one year, so a lost claim becomes a charge and a delayed collection together. The third-quarter report states this split, which corrects the earlier Business & governance statement that it is not stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 32–33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8–9, 56; calculation C18; calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

Cash generation is strong but partly customer funded, so it should not be capitalised as a stable base. Operating cash flow was USD 665,063 thousand in the first nine months of 2026, of which USD 249,832 thousand came from working-capital inflows, and in FY2024 operating cash flow of USD 503,544 thousand was more than all working capital, since before it the figure was USD -85,580 thousand. After capital expenditure of USD 91,265 thousand the nine-month figure was USD 573,798 thousand, before USD 23,800 thousand paid to joint venture partners and USD 41,202 thousand of dividends and repurchases. Capital intensity is low at 1.92% of revenue, but FY2025 spending of USD 180,854 thousand was 3.26% of revenue and 3.80x depreciation on owner-funded equipment for newer projects, so capital expenditure is flexible but not zero. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 48, 71–72; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13

Liquidity is strong against every maturity and against the known cash calls, but nearly a quarter of the general-purpose cash is already claimed by share awards. At 2026-09-30 cash available for general corporate purposes of USD 504,218 thousand plus the undrawn USD 350,000 thousand revolver is USD 854,218 thousand, while USD 606,831 thousand, or 54.62% of reported cash, is joint venture cash that creditors cannot count on. Cash-settled share awards are liabilities of USD 120.9 million, up from USD 85.2 million at the end of 2025 even after USD 31.0 million paid in nine months, and equal to 23.98% of general-purpose cash; management says most remaining awards of this kind vest by the end of 2026, and the filings do not say when the cash is paid. The Philadelphia hotel award adds a contingent USD 175 million, or 34.71% of the same cash. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10, 25, 28, 61; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C28; calculation C17

Financial policy has shifted from repair to returns, which is acceptable at this leverage but has not been tested by a downturn. The first lien leverage covenant needed two amendments in 2022 and 2023 and FY2024 ended in a loss; since then the term loan was repaid early, dividends began in December 2025 and USD 30,000 thousand of shares were bought back, leaving USD 170 million of authorisation. Returns were 6.20% of nine-month operating cash flow and gross debt is 22.69% of total capitalisation; no sponsor sits above the company, the executive chairman and related trusts hold about 12% and may nominate a director, and alignment therefore has to be judged from conduct, which so far shows returns well below operating cash flow. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 67; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C21; calculation C22

Refinancing risk is low until 2031, and the one market price supplied does not signal distress, though it is below par. The July 2026 refinancing replaced the 2029 notes with USD 400.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 2033 and lifted the secured revolver to USD 350.0 million, undrawn and maturing in 2031, at a cash premium of USD 35.6 million that the issuer-stated USD 21.0 million of annual interest saving repays in 1.70 years; management also states that interest income exceeded interest expense from the third quarter of 2026 and expects that to continue. The 2033 notes were valued at USD 390.0 million, or 97.50% of principal, at 2026-09-30, which implies a yield above the coupon, and no peer prices are supplied to say whether that is wide; the revolver's two maintenance tests, reported at -0.22x against a 3.50x maximum and 17.14x against a 3.00x minimum, apply only to the revolver and follow definitions that are not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–18, 34, 62, 66; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C27

runs.text: Strength: net cash and a long maturity profile. At 2026-09-30 gross debt of USD 403,641 thousand is 1.02x last-twelve-months EBITDA and 22.69% of total capitalisation, general-purpose cash of USD 504,218 thousand exceeds it, and the only large maturity is the 2033 notes, so over the next two years default would have to come from execution and litigation losses rather than from a debt wall, and a refinancing is not needed to stay liquid. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10, 14–18; calculation C23; calculation C22; calculation C14

Strength: contracted, publicly funded backlog. Backlog of USD 20,353.3 million is 3.25 years of revenue and firm obligations are 2.78x, public agencies were 73.82% of nine-month 2026 revenue and Civil carries a 14.0% margin, so revenue and the most profitable segment are visible for about three years, which supports debt service even if new awards slow for a few quarters. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 49–50, 55–56; calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C5

Strength: lower fixed charges and light covenants. The 2026 refinancing cut interest expense to USD 34,407 thousand for nine months from USD 41,489 thousand, the issuer-stated annual saving is USD 21.0 million, management states that interest income has exceeded interest expense since the third quarter of 2026, and the only maintenance tests apply to an undrawn revolver, so fixed charges and default triggers are lower than a year ago and a covenant breach is a remote route to default. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 15–18, 62, 66; calculation C26; calculation C27

Strength: improving earnings power in the largest segment. Operating margin reached 6.37% in nine months against -2.40% in FY2024, driven by volume on larger projects, so earnings, not asset sales, are building the cash that covers the debt. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 55–56; calculation C2; calculation C4

Weakness: fixed-price execution and recurring disputes. Fixed-price work was 79% of backlog at the end of 2025, legal judgments and settlements cost USD 213.5 million in FY2024 and USD 94.3 million in FY2025, and claims plus unapproved change orders of USD 687,916 thousand exceed general-purpose cash, so overruns and lost claims fall on the company and a single dispute can swing a year, as a USD 101.6 million adjustment for an arbitration ruling on a completed California bridge project did in FY2024, which makes earnings the least predictable part of the credit. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 32–33, 86; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C18; calculation C10

Weakness: the Philadelphia hotel award. The court awarded about USD 175 million, 34.71% of general-purpose cash and 44.13% of last-twelve-months EBITDA, a second ruling adds USD 42 million, and in October 2026, after the balance sheet date, the trial court denied the company's indemnity claims against its concrete subcontractor and that subcontractor's surety, which narrows the recovery available, so a loss on appeal would be the largest single contingent cash call in the filings, fundable from cash but large enough to change how much room remains for returns and projects. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–26; calculation C17

Weakness: customer-funded working capital. Billings in excess of costs of USD 2,044,207 thousand are 5.06x gross debt and 37.57% of nine-month operating cash flow came from working capital, so cash generation depends on advances that reverse if awards stop replacing revenue, and a return of advances outside the joint ventures to their end-2024 level would absorb USD 587,370 thousand. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; calculation C24; calculation C11; calculation C20

Weakness: slowing backlog replacement and unsettled funding. Awards were 0.96x revenue, backlog is down 5.77% on a year earlier, and the federal infrastructure funding window closed on 2026-09-30 with authorisations extended only to 2026-12-11, so growth in visibility is not assured and the sector tailwind depends on legislation not yet passed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50, 53; calculation C6; calculation C7

Weakness: financial policy that depends on documents not seen. Cash-settled share awards of USD 120.9 million, a USD 170 million repurchase authorisation and an executive chairman with about 12% and a board nomination right all compete for the same cash, and without the executed debt documents the limit on payouts cannot be read, so the policy dimension is held at average. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C16; calculation C21; Business & governance (CP-1A)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The only new debt issue in the period is the refinancing completed on 2026-07-02. The company issued USD 400.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 2033, used the proceeds with cash to redeem in full the USD 400.0 million of senior notes due 2029 at 108.906% of principal, and amended and restated its credit agreement so that the revolver grew from USD 170.0 million to USD 350.0 million with maturity extended to 2031. The old first lien net leverage covenant was replaced by a maximum total net leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio that apply only to the revolver. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–17

The refinancing cost a loss on extinguishment of USD 51.4 million, of which USD 35.6 million was cash premium and USD 15.8 million was non-cash write-off of unamortised costs, and the company states annualised cash interest savings of USD 21.0 million, so the premium is repaid in 1.70 years if the saving holds. The new notes carry the same subsidiary guarantees as the credit agreement and the revolver stays secured by substantially all assets; the filings describe no change in lien priority and no priming or non-pro-rata step. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–18, 62; calculation C10

Other capital events in the period are not new debt: the remaining term loan was repaid early in the first quarter of 2025, the defined benefit pension plan was settled in the third quarter of 2026 with a USD 33.8 million non-cash charge, and no acquisition, disposal or sponsor transaction is described in any of the five documents. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 62

The third-quarter report lists the July 2026 indenture and the amended and restated credit agreement as exhibits incorporated by reference to a current report filed on 2026-07-06, and the annual report does the same for the 2024 indenture, so guarantor, security, covenant, default and redemption terms can be read only as the filings summarise them. fields.value: Nothing dated after 2026-11-04 is supplied, which is 14 days before the as-of date. No later current report, earnings release, investor presentation or market update is in the evidence, so any event between those dates is not established. The third-quarter report has no separate subsequent-events note; the one post-quarter development it describes is the October 2026 ruling in which the trial court denied the company's indemnity claims against its concrete subcontractor and that subcontractor's surety in the Philadelphia hotel dispute.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No filing prints EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA. The term appears only in the credit agreement's incremental-debt basket tests, whose definition is not supplied, and the non-GAAP measures printed are adjusted net income attributable to the company and adjusted diluted earnings per share. Leverage and coverage on an EBITDA basis must be built from statement lines and will not match the covenant ratios, which the filings report only as finished ratios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The covenant measures are not a continuous series. Through the first quarter of 2026 the revolver was tested on a maximum first lien net leverage ratio; the amended agreement replaced that test with a maximum total net leverage ratio and a minimum cash interest coverage ratio, first tested at the end of the second quarter of 2026, and the second-quarter report prints both sets of tests. Ratios reported before the amendment are therefore on a different definition from the current ones.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported cash includes joint venture cash. Of the cash and cash equivalents at 2026-09-30, the portion available for general corporate purposes is stated separately; the remainder is held by consolidated joint ventures and by the company's share of unconsolidated joint ventures and is available only for joint venture uses. Any liquidity or leverage view has to use the general-purpose figure, which is also the cash the covenant definitions offset against indebtedness.

fields.value: Cash generation is strong but is flattered by customer funding. fields.value: Tutor Perini is a public-company contractor whose creditors depend on project execution and public customers, not on a sponsor, and the filings document no creditor-adverse conduct, though the debt documents that would show what owners may take out are not supplied.

fields.value: Public agencies were 74.69% of FY2025 revenue and fixed-price work is 79% of backlog, so margins turn on execution and on settling change orders. fields.value: - Revenue visibility is strong but rests on a few large public projects. fields.value: - Margins depend on fixed-price execution and on collecting claims. Fixed-price work is 69.39% of FY2025 revenue and 79% of backlog, customers may terminate government contracts for convenience, and unapproved change orders and claims sit in costs and estimated earnings in excess of billings of USD 767,432 thousand, so a lost claim becomes a cash and earnings shock rather than a delay.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer advances and bonding are the funding model, not debt. Billings in excess of costs of USD 2,044,207 thousand fund projects ahead of spending, and surety bonds are needed to win work, so a slowdown in awards or a loss of bonding capacity would hit liquidity before it hits leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Control is a listed-company board with one influential holder, not a sponsor. The Tutor Group holds about 12% and may nominate one director while it holds at least 11.25%, ten directors signed the annual report, and no fund, fund vintage or exit horizon is described to infer pressure from, so alignment has to be judged from conduct rather than identity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Financial policy has moved from covenant relief to returns, and the evidence so far is mixed rather than adverse. Two covenant amendments were needed in 2022 and 2023, the term loan was repaid early in 2025, dividends began in December 2025, USD 30,000 thousand of shares were repurchased in nine months of 2026 with USD 170 million of authorisation left, and the 2026 refinancing cost a USD 35.6 million premium that the issuer-stated USD 21.0 million annual saving repays in 1.70 years.

fields.value: - The Philadelphia hotel dispute is the one live item that could change the picture. The court awarded the developer approximately USD 175 million, the company has appealed, and management describes a material adverse impact as neither probable nor remote.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a moderate governance risk reading is the covenant record and the dispute record: the first lien leverage covenant needed two amendments within five months in 2022 and 2023, FY2024 ended in a loss with legacy-dispute charges, and a court awarded approximately USD 175 million, equal to 34.71% of the USD 504,218 thousand of general-purpose cash. The strongest evidence for the opposite, a lower-risk reading, is that distributions were only 6.20% of nine-month 2026 operating cash flow and that the 2026 refinancing lowered interest cost and extended maturity without any documented priming.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would worsen if the appeal fails and the award is paid from general-purpose cash, if the indenture or credit agreement prove to allow large restricted payments, or if repurchases accelerate while backlog keeps falling. It would improve if the documents show tight restricted-payment limits and the appeal reduces the award.

fields.value: The only new debt issue in the period is the refinancing completed on 2026-07-02. The company issued USD 400.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 2033, used the proceeds with cash to redeem in full the USD 400.0 million of senior notes due 2029 at 108.906% of principal, and amended and restated its credit agreement so that the revolver grew from USD 170.0 million to USD 350.0 million with maturity extended to 2031. The old first lien net leverage covenant was replaced by a maximum total net leverage ratio and a minimum interest coverage ratio that apply only to the revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The refinancing cost a loss on extinguishment of USD 51.4 million, of which USD 35.6 million was cash premium and USD 15.8 million was non-cash write-off of unamortised costs, and the company states annualised cash interest savings of USD 21.0 million, so the premium is repaid in 1.70 years if the saving holds. The new notes carry the same subsidiary guarantees as the credit agreement and the revolver stays secured by substantially all assets; the filings describe no change in lien priority and no priming or non-pro-rata step.

Scope: business risk, financial profile, outlook, downside and monitoring from the 2024 and 2025 annual reports and the three 2026 quarterly reports, built on the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance results. No rating, relative-value, recovery or covenant-capacity view is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tutor Perini has an adequate and improving credit profile: gross debt is covered by cash and no debt of size falls due before 2033, so creditors are exposed mainly to fixed-price project execution and one court award, not to refinancing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 14–18; calculation C23; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: At 2026-09-30 gross debt is 1.02x last-twelve-months EBITDA, USD 504,218 thousand of general-purpose cash plus the undrawn USD 350,000 thousand revolver gives USD 854,218 thousand of liquidity, and backlog of USD 20,353.3 million is 3.25x last-twelve-months revenue. The weak points are earnings that were a loss in FY2024 on legal charges, a USD 175 million Philadelphia hotel award under appeal that equals 34.71% of general-purpose cash, and customer advances of USD 2,044,207 thousand that fund the business and would reverse if awards stopped keeping pace with revenue. Awards were 0.96x revenue in the first nine months of 2026, so backlog replacement and claims collection are what to watch.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10, 25, 49–50; calculation C23; calculation C14; calculation C7; calculation C17; calculation C24; calculation C6; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business profile is adequate: large and scaled in work where few firms compete, but concentrated in a handful of big fixed-price public projects. Last-twelve-months revenue is USD 6,254,126 thousand, public agencies were 73.82% of nine-month 2026 revenue, and two customers with multiple projects made up 24.1% of it, at 13.3% and 10.8%; the third-quarter report names the second customer, so the earlier Business & governance figure of one customer at 10.8% understates concentration. Management says fewer firms now bid on the largest civil projects, which helps pricing but cannot be tested because no market-share figure is supplied. A funding delay or a dispute on one large project therefore moves earnings and cash more than the revenue base suggests, so scale is a strength and concentration is the matching weakness.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 44, 49–50; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 124; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C7; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is visible for about three years, but the pipeline that feeds it has stopped growing. Nine-month 2026 new awards of USD 4,540.3 million were 0.96x revenue recognised, against USD 7.0 billion in the same period of 2025, and backlog is down 5.77% on a year earlier although up from USD 19.9 billion at the end of the second quarter. Firm remaining performance obligations, which exclude unexercised options, are USD 17.4 billion, 2.78x revenue and down only 2.79% on a year earlier, so the firm base is steadier than the headline backlog. Management attributes the fall to an unusually strong 2025 and fewer large awards reaching decision in 2026, and points to a pipeline above USD 200 billion over three to four years and a multi-billion-dollar California healthcare project to be added within two years; these are expectations, not bookings. Backlog equal to 3.25 years of revenue protects earnings in the near term, but sustained awards below revenue would shrink it and the customer advances attached to it.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 49–50, 52–53, 58; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin recovery is real but comes from volume and lower stock-linked pay rather than better gross margins, so it is less secure than the headline suggests. Income from construction operations moved from a margin of -2.40% in FY2024 to 4.18% in FY2025 and 6.37% in the first nine months of 2026, yet gross margin was 12.37% against 12.38% a year earlier; of the USD 120,487 thousand rise in operating income, 72.69% came from higher gross profit on 17.62% more revenue and the rest from lower general and administrative cost as share-based pay fell by USD 43.5 million. Civil earned a 14.0% margin against 4.8% in Building and 2.1% in Specialty Contractors, so Civil execution carries the credit.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 42–43, 47, 55–60; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disputes are a recurring cost of this business model, not a one-off, and unproven claims decide how much profit turns into cash. Legal judgments and settlements cost USD 213.5 million in FY2024 and USD 94.3 million in FY2025, which is 40.65% of FY2025 income from construction operations, and a USD 16.4 million adverse change on a California transit project in the first quarter of 2026 came from change-order negotiations that management says were later settled with the owner and should bring cash. Fixed-price work was 79% of backlog at the end of 2025, and claims plus unapproved change orders of USD 687,916 thousand are 89.64% of the USD 767,432 thousand of costs in excess of billings and 136.43% of general-purpose cash, with management expecting about USD 521.4 million of that balance to be collected beyond one year, so a lost claim becomes a charge and a delayed collection together. The third-quarter report states this split, which corrects the earlier Business & governance statement that it is not stated.

fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 32–33; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8–9, 56; calculation C18; calculation C10; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is strong but partly customer funded, so it should not be capitalised as a stable base. Operating cash flow was USD 665,063 thousand in the first nine months of 2026, of which USD 249,832 thousand came from working-capital inflows, and in FY2024 operating cash flow of USD 503,544 thousand was more than all working capital, since before it the figure was USD -85,580 thousand. After capital expenditure of USD 91,265 thousand the nine-month figure was USD 573,798 thousand, before USD 23,800 thousand paid to joint venture partners and USD 41,202 thousand of dividends and repurchases. Capital intensity is low at 1.92% of revenue, but FY2025 spending of USD 180,854 thousand was 3.26% of revenue and 3.80x depreciation on owner-funded equipment for newer projects, so capital expenditure is flexible but not zero.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 48, 71–72; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C11; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is strong against every maturity and against the known cash calls, but nearly a quarter of the general-purpose cash is already claimed by share awards. At 2026-09-30 cash available for general corporate purposes of USD 504,218 thousand plus the undrawn USD 350,000 thousand revolver is USD 854,218 thousand, while USD 606,831 thousand, or 54.62% of reported cash, is joint venture cash that creditors cannot count on. Cash-settled share awards are liabilities of USD 120.9 million, up from USD 85.2 million at the end of 2025 even after USD 31.0 million paid in nine months, and equal to 23.98% of general-purpose cash; management says most remaining awards of this kind vest by the end of 2026, and the filings do not say when the cash is paid. The Philadelphia hotel award adds a contingent USD 175 million, or 34.71% of the same cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy has shifted from repair to returns, which is acceptable at this leverage but has not been tested by a downturn. The first lien leverage covenant needed two amendments in 2022 and 2023 and FY2024 ended in a loss; since then the term loan was repaid early, dividends began in December 2025 and USD 30,000 thousand of shares were bought back, leaving USD 170 million of authorisation. Returns were 6.20% of nine-month operating cash flow and gross debt is 22.69% of total capitalisation; no sponsor sits above the company, the executive chairman and related trusts hold about 12% and may nominate a director, and alignment therefore has to be judged from conduct, which so far shows returns well below operating cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 26–27, 52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 67; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C21; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Refinancing risk is low until 2031, and the one market price supplied does not signal distress, though it is below par. The July 2026 refinancing replaced the 2029 notes with USD 400.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 2033 and lifted the secured revolver to USD 350.0 million, undrawn and maturing in 2031, at a cash premium of USD 35.6 million that the issuer-stated USD 21.0 million of annual interest saving repays in 1.70 years; management also states that interest income exceeded interest expense from the third quarter of 2026 and expects that to continue. The 2033 notes were valued at USD 390.0 million, or 97.50% of principal, at 2026-09-30, which implies a yield above the coupon, and no peer prices are supplied to say whether that is wide; the revolver's two maintenance tests, reported at -0.22x against a 3.50x maximum and 17.14x against a 3.00x minimum, apply only to the revolver and follow definitions that are not supplied.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–18, 34, 62, 66; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C25; calculation C26; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against an adequate and improving view is that the improvement is recent and leans on items that may not repeat: FY2024 EBITDA was negative, 44.20% of FY2025 operating cash flow came from working-capital inflows, awards are below revenue, legal and settlement charges have recurred in both years, and the Philadelphia award equals 44.13% of last-twelve-months EBITDA. The strongest evidence for a better view than adequate is that consolidated net debt is -1.78x EBITDA, general-purpose cash alone exceeds gross debt, and a cash call of USD 337,900 thousand from the award, the window wall ruling and the share awards would still leave USD 516,318 thousand of liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would worsen if the appeal fails while awards stay below revenue and billings in excess of costs start to fall, if unapproved change orders are written down, or if repurchases accelerate while backlog shrinks. It would improve if awards exceed revenue for several quarters, the appeal cuts the award, claims on the California transit and other projects convert to cash, and the debt documents show tight limits on payouts.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 8, 25–26, 28, 49–50; calculation C6; calculation C10; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No agency rating, peer set or dated bond quote beyond one period-end fair value is supplied, so the adequate business-profile conclusion is absolute rather than relative to other contractors and the financial-policy and refinancing conclusions cannot be calibrated against how the market prices comparable credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The amount of recovery carried in receivables for the Philadelphia hotel project is not stated, so the earnings effect of losing the appeal cannot be separated from the cash payment, and the downside case treats the full award as cash only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Dates for paying the cash-settled share awards and any appeal bond or collateral needed to stay the Philadelphia award are not stated, so the timing of the largest known cash calls in the downside case is an assumption.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The pipeline above USD 200 billion and the timing of the California healthcare project are management expectations without dates or probabilities, so the medium-term outlook leans on language the filings do not evidence and is held at adequate rather than strong.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The leverage and cover figures use EBITDA built after stock-linked pay and the covenant ratios use definitions that are not supplied, so the financial-profile conclusion could move by the size of the stock-linked charge, which was USD 77,179 thousand in nine months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 66; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C29

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: net cash and a long maturity profile. At 2026-09-30 gross debt of USD 403,641 thousand is 1.02x last-twelve-months EBITDA and 22.69% of total capitalisation, general-purpose cash of USD 504,218 thousand exceeds it, and the only large maturity is the 2033 notes, so over the next two years default would have to come from execution and litigation losses rather than from a debt wall, and a refinancing is not needed to stay liquid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10, 14–18; calculation C23; calculation C22; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: contracted, publicly funded backlog. Backlog of USD 20,353.3 million is 3.25 years of revenue and firm obligations are 2.78x, public agencies were 73.82% of nine-month 2026 revenue and Civil carries a 14.0% margin, so revenue and the most profitable segment are visible for about three years, which supports debt service even if new awards slow for a few quarters.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 49–50, 55–56; calculation C7; calculation C9; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: lower fixed charges and light covenants. The 2026 refinancing cut interest expense to USD 34,407 thousand for nine months from USD 41,489 thousand, the issuer-stated annual saving is USD 21.0 million, management states that interest income has exceeded interest expense since the third quarter of 2026, and the only maintenance tests apply to an undrawn revolver, so fixed charges and default triggers are lower than a year ago and a covenant breach is a remote route to default.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 15–18, 62, 66; calculation C26; calculation C27

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strength: improving earnings power in the largest segment. Operating margin reached 6.37% in nine months against -2.40% in FY2024, driven by volume on larger projects, so earnings, not asset sales, are building the cash that covers the debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 55–56; calculation C2; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: fixed-price execution and recurring disputes. Fixed-price work was 79% of backlog at the end of 2025, legal judgments and settlements cost USD 213.5 million in FY2024 and USD 94.3 million in FY2025, and claims plus unapproved change orders of USD 687,916 thousand exceed general-purpose cash, so overruns and lost claims fall on the company and a single dispute can swing a year, as a USD 101.6 million adjustment for an arbitration ruling on a completed California bridge project did in FY2024, which makes earnings the least predictable part of the credit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 32–33, 86; 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C18; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: the Philadelphia hotel award. The court awarded about USD 175 million, 34.71% of general-purpose cash and 44.13% of last-twelve-months EBITDA, a second ruling adds USD 42 million, and in October 2026, after the balance sheet date, the trial court denied the company's indemnity claims against its concrete subcontractor and that subcontractor's surety, which narrows the recovery available, so a loss on appeal would be the largest single contingent cash call in the filings, fundable from cash but large enough to change how much room remains for returns and projects.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: customer-funded working capital. Billings in excess of costs of USD 2,044,207 thousand are 5.06x gross debt and 37.57% of nine-month operating cash flow came from working capital, so cash generation depends on advances that reverse if awards stop replacing revenue, and a return of advances outside the joint ventures to their end-2024 level would absorb USD 587,370 thousand.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; calculation C24; calculation C11; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: slowing backlog replacement and unsettled funding. Awards were 0.96x revenue, backlog is down 5.77% on a year earlier, and the federal infrastructure funding window closed on 2026-09-30 with authorisations extended only to 2026-12-11, so growth in visibility is not assured and the sector tailwind depends on legislation not yet passed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 49–50, 53; calculation C6; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weakness: financial policy that depends on documents not seen. Cash-settled share awards of USD 120.9 million, a USD 170 million repurchase authorisation and an executive chairman with about 12% and a board nomination right all compete for the same cash, and without the executed debt documents the limit on payouts cannot be read, so the policy dimension is held at average.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C16; calculation C21; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next one to two years earnings should hold or improve while cash is drawn on by known items. The large projects now in execution have substantial scope remaining, backlog rose from USD 19.9 billion at the end of the second quarter to USD 20,353.3 million, annual cash interest is expected to fall by the issuer-stated USD 21.0 million, and management projects lower stock-linked pay in 2026 and a much larger fall in 2027. Against that, the Philadelphia appeal, the share award settlements and the repurchase authorisation of USD 170 million could all draw on the same USD 504,218 thousand of general-purpose cash, so liquidity should stay ample but shrink before it grows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25–28, 47–50, 61–62, 67; calculation C7; calculation C26; calculation C16; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the outlook turns on funding that is not settled. The federal infrastructure law funding window closed on 2026-09-30 and surface-transportation authorisations were extended only to 2026-12-11 while a USD 580 billion reauthorisation bill is negotiated; management states that most major projects rely more on state and local funding, cites USD 41.4 billion of voter-approved transportation measures from November 2024, and points to defence funding in Guam and the Indo-Pacific. These are management statements and the filings give no probability or timing for reauthorisation, so a funding gap would first show as slower awards and shrinking customer advances rather than as a debt problem.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive and cost forces matter to creditors mainly through bidding and margin. Management says few firms bid on the largest fixed-price civil projects, which supports awards and pricing, while customers are mostly public agencies that can end contracts for convenience and buy by competitive bid, so buyer power is high on smaller jobs and lower on the largest. Cost inflation and tariffs are managed by buying out materials, taking fixed-price quotes from subcontractors and pricing escalation into bids, which shifts much of the risk to suppliers but not all of it; about 4,000 employees are union members with wage escalation priced into bids. Technology and social factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside is a loss on the Philadelphia appeal combined with awards that stay below revenue, which hits cash before it hits leverage. First, the court award of about USD 175 million and the USD 42 million window wall ruling are upheld and the share awards settle in cash, a cash call of USD 337,900 thousand that leaves USD 166,318 thousand of general-purpose cash and USD 516,318 thousand of liquidity with the revolver, and net debt on general-purpose cash of USD 237,323 thousand, or 0.60x last-twelve-months EBITDA. Second, awards below revenue stop the growth of customer advances; a return of the advances outside joint ventures to their end-2024 level would absorb a further USD 587,370 thousand, 68.76% of the original liquidity, which together with the first call, USD 925,270 thousand, would exceed the original USD 854,218 thousand of liquidity, but that needs several years of shrinking awards and is the tail, not the base case.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue would not fall quickly because backlog covers about three years, and margins would be pressured by further adverse adjustments like the USD 16.4 million recorded in the first quarter of 2026 and by the loss of the recovery carried on the hotel project. Management levers are the undrawn revolver, the discretionary repurchase authorisation, dividends of USD 5.0 million declared in the third quarter, the timing of equipment purchases and distributions to joint venture partners. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in the first case; distress needs the combined tail, and the covenants apply only to the revolver, so a breach would first affect revolver access, and whether it would reach the notes depends on cross-default terms that are not supplied. Each 10% of claims and unapproved change orders that is not collected would cost USD 68,792 thousand of earnings and cash. These figures are arithmetic on stated amounts, not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_tpc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 4, 10, 25–28, 49–50, 56, 67; 10-K_2025-12-31_tpc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; calculation C19; calculation C20; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Tutor Perini presents an adequate business profile supported by a USD 20,353.3 million backlog, public customers and a refinanced balance sheet, but credit quality is constrained by fixed-price execution risk, recurring dispute charges and customer-funded working capital. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because operating cash flow before working capital was USD 415,231 thousand in nine months, although it is flattered by customer advances that cannot be assumed to grow. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings holding near current levels and on bond market access as the 2033 notes approach maturity, since nothing of size matures sooner. The primary downside path is a loss on the Philadelphia appeal combined with awards below revenue and shrinking customer advances. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, the covenant definitions, the collection timetable for claims and unapproved change orders, the recovery carried on the hotel project and market prices for comparison. The top risk is backlog replacement failing while claims remain uncollected.
